subject: infra.connect

subject: infra.connect

note: No coverage obligation, duration or universal-service term is stated in the held account

subject: infra.connect

position_start: Licensed and operating; local resale permitted from January 2025

note: Licence terms, fee and duration are not held

subject: infra.connect
name: State mobile operator turnaround plan

position_start: US$40m loss in 2022; US$160m revenue projected for 2024

subject: infra.connect
name: State operator's satellite reseller revenue

note: Operator-reported

subject: infra.connect

subject: infra.connect
name: Uncapped fibre package at US$99

position_start: Two fixed operators cut prices and introduced unlimited packages in August 2025
position_end: Priced against the satellite operator's US$100 plan; the incumbent's fixed-traffic share fell from 58.90% in Q3 2025 to 48.41% in Q4 2025
note: Prices are the operators' own, in United States dollars

subject: infra.store
name: Commercial data centre capacity
milestone: Analyst estimates as of 2024, published July 2025
position_end: About six live commercial facilities carrying roughly 2 MW of live critical information technology load, about 2.5 MW in construction, about 40% occupancy and about US$4m of annual commercial revenue, with none of the supply carrier-neutral

subject: infra.store
name: National data centre ecosystem
milestone: Committed in the ICT minister's five-point policy compass
position_end: Committed, with a national high-performance computing centre, the state fixed operator and a private operator's data centre named as the spine; no capacity, cost or completion date
note: Part-financing stated as a ring-fenced share of the universal services fund, amount not stated; the ministry's own 2025 priority-projects page already carried this as item 03, describing it as consolidating government data storage and improving data management and security, with no downloadable priority document served

subject: infra.store
name: National high-performance computing centre
milestone: Phase 2 grant of CNY 100,000,000 signed 2017-12-06, implementation from 2018
position_start: Operating; no utilisation or capacity figure held for 2025
position_end: Named as part of the national infrastructural spine (2026-07-29); a developer account reports access quoted in tens of thousands of United States dollars in large blocks
note: Phase 2 was to raise capacity from 36 to over 300 teraflops; no delivered figure is held

subject: infra.store
name: Operator artificial-intelligence service
milestone: Launched 2026-04-15; the operator states the compute is hosted in South Africa
position_end: Operating, with consulting and Shona-language work and a stated sovereign cloud offer to government; the operator's own announcement places the compute at an affiliated group's facility in South Africa
note: The siting is stated first-hand in the operator's launch announcement

subject: infra.store
name: Sovereign national cloud
milestone: Provided for in the National AI Strategy 2026-2030, launched 2026-03-13
position_end: Provided for in the strategy, with high-performance computing centres formalised as national assets and agricultural predictive models and geological maps to be held on domestic servers; no site, capacity, cost or date published

note: A media rights organisation records that the strategy has no legal force; a proposed act is named as the instrument that would supply residency rules

subject: infra.store
name: State or government data centre inventory
milestone: TelOne's own product page states its facility is a Tier 3 Data Centre Environment, the operator's own undated claim, not certified or dated
position_start: Not held; the state operator's annual report was quoted only saying the data centre business continued to grow
position_end: TelOne states its data centre environment is Tier 3 standard (operator's own undated claim, not certified), vendor- and ICT-provider-neutral, running Microsoft HyperV, VMware, OpenStack and Huawei FusionSphere virtual-machine platforms with active-active redundancy across multiple data centres nationally, and positioned explicitly for government-to-citizen interactions; no capacity, utilisation or site-count figure published
note: Tier 3 claim is the operator's own undated marketing claim

subject: infra.store
name: Technology park and data centre, Harare
milestone: Groundbreaking expected in the fourth quarter of the financial year
position_end: A 300-hectare park near the international airport with a 100 MW solar plant and a data centre of undisclosed capacity; phase 1 of the solar farm under construction

subject: infra.energy

position_end: Phase 1 under construction; phase 1 capacity, cost, financing and completion date all unstated
note: Company-reported

subject: infra.energy
name: Artificial-intelligence fuel management on tower sites
milestone: Phased rollout reported for the quarter to May 2026

note: Company-reported

subject: infra.energy
name: Base-station solar programme
milestone: Solar systems deployed across new and existing sites in the quarter to May 2026

note: Company-reported

subject: infra.energy

position_start: Licensed since 2018; no later capacity disclosure held
position_end: Generation Licence GC0066/2018 authorises a 0.45 MW grid-connected solar plant at Willowvale for own consumption; no installed megawatts, site count or tariff published since
note: The licence is the mobile operator's; the capacity of the power arm now inside the infrastructure company is not held

subject: infra.energy
name: Solar for Health programme
milestone: 1,044 health facilities solarised across all ten provinces (2025-08)
position_end: 1,044 health facilities solarised across all ten provinces, more than 60% of all facilities, on 11 megawatts of installed capacity and more than US$28m of financing; power is stated as the precondition for connectivity and electronic records
note: Figures are the health financing partner's own

subject: infra.capacity
name: Equipped international internet bandwidth
milestone: Regulator's Q4 2025 sector report

subject: infra.capacity
name: National internet exchange point
milestone: Reported to the ITU Regional Development Forum for Africa 2020-10-06
position_start: Operating and reported to the ITU in 2020; no later statement held
position_end: The Harare Internet Exchange Point, built on a US$200,000 African Union Commission grant and housed in the state fixed operator's exchange building, with every Zimbabwean access provider connected and two international peers (2020-10)
note: No traffic, peering or membership figure later than October 2020 is held

subject: infra.capacity
name: Regulator's international bandwidth measurement framework
milestone: The satellite operator excluded and the baseline restated from Q2 2025
position_start: The operator excluded and the baseline restated from Q2 2025, after Q1 2025 used bandwidth of 2.69 Tbps exceeded equipped capacity of 1.43 Tbps
position_end: The same basis at Q4 2025; the carrier that accounted for 35.05% of fixed traffic has no domestic ground infrastructure to measure
note: The apparent collapse in headline used bandwidth is a reclassification, not a fall in traffic

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Artificial-intelligence and cybersecurity fusion centre
milestone: Proposed in the National AI Strategy 2026-2030
position_end: Proposed for real-time threat detection; a media rights organisation reports that the strategy sets out no governance structure, no limits on data collection, retention or use, and no route to challenge a threat assessment
sources: 2026-06-23 Implications of Zimbabwe’s National AI Strategy on Freedom of Expression Privacy and Access to Information|2026-03-16-ai-strategy-mandates-local-storage
note: The strategy has no legal force

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cyber risk in the payment system, central bank assessment
position_end: Vulnerabilities flagged by the Reserve Bank in third-party providers, payment channels and digital banking, alongside 36% of deployed card terminals active and 586,605 internet-banking subscribers (2026-08)
note: from the governor's mid-term monetary policy statement, which urges AI-assisted fraud detection and the elimination of ghost accounts; no incident count, loss figure or breach series accompanies the assessment, so the risk is asserted by the supervisor without being sized. The one hard number in it is about capacity rather than security - only 36% of deployed point-of-sale terminals are active

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cyber security and monitoring of interception of communications centre
milestone: Established as a unit in the Office of the President by the Cyber and Data Protection Act
position_start: Operating under the Office of the President, advised by a committee on warrants, with no judicial oversight
position_end: Same; a media rights organisation reported in June 2026 that the centre still has no judicial oversight
sources: 2022-03-11-zimbabwe-cyber-and-data-protection-act-chapter-12-07|2026-06-23 Implications of Zimbabwe’s National AI Strategy on Freedom of Expression Privacy and Access to Information
note: The Act amends the interception statute to create it; the Act's long title and the organisation's account name the body differently

subject: infra.cybersec

milestone: Reported as established alongside the National Cybersecurity Strategy

subject: infra.cybersec

The model Data Sharing Agreement gives the United States secure, uninterrupted access, expressly including login credentials, to seven national health systems including electronic medical records, for twenty-five years continuing ten years past termination — and in the same clause tells the partner that to the maximum extent practical it should not provide individual level data or personally identifiable information unless there is no other way, the model access role being a viewer role without access to such information. The template memorandum's section 2.1.2 requires physical specimens and related data, including genetic sequence data, of detected pathogens with epidemic potential to be provided within five days of detection for twenty-five years. Both public accounts are therefore supportable on the templates: Harare is describing standing credentialled access to live national systems and specimen transfer, Washington is denying the transfer of identifiable records. subject: digital.localgov
name: Local authority electronic services and revenue systems
milestone: Kwekwe City Council's own page states billing runs on the Promun (ERP) package
movement: No change, one council documented against an unchanged national picture
position_start: Most councils lagging in technology on the Auditor-General’s FY2024 audits, with business processes still manual or partially automated, accounting-system modules left unactivated, and most authorities without an enterprise resource planning system for revenue collection and so recognising revenue on a cash basis for want of complete databases; revenue-collection and debt-recovery findings rose from 81 across 51 local authorities to 92 across 60 (2025-06)
position_end: Kwekwe City Council bills rates, refuse, sewerage, water and other service charges centrally through the Promun (ERP) package, with each property assigned a unique account number and tariff code; the finance department names "Information Technology and E-Governance" among its five key functions, covering database administration, network security and system workflow; legal basis is the Urban Councils Act s.219 for rates and the Water Act [Chapter 20:22] and Environmental Management Act [Chapter 20:17] for service charges; no user count, collection rate or digital-channel adoption figure published
note: the closing position is one council’s own statement and is not established as representative; no national follow-up audit of local-authority automation is held
